oil.when: 2003 trucks with the Driver Information Center (information and select buttons)
steps: Reset only after the engine oil and filter have actually been changed.
Turn the ignition on.
Press the information button until ENGINE OIL LIFE shows in the display.
While ENGINE OIL LIFE is showing, press and hold the select button until the reading goes back to 100%.
oil.note: The oil life reading does not measure how much oil is in the engine, so keep checking the dipstick between changes.

steps: Reset only after the engine oil and filter have actually been changed.
Turn the key to RUN with the engine off.
Push the accelerator pedal all the way down and let it up, three times within five seconds.
OIL LIFE RESET should flash for about 10 seconds while the system resets.
Turn the key to LOCK. If CHANGE ENGINE OIL comes back on at the next start, repeat the steps; if it still will not clear, have a dealer look at it.

oil.when: 2009–2012 trucks with Driver Information Center buttons
steps: Reset only after the engine oil and filter have actually been changed.
Turn the ignition on and use the DIC buttons to bring up OIL LIFE REMAINING.
Press and hold the SET/RESET button for more than five seconds.
Let go when the oil life reads 100%. If CHANGE ENGINE OIL SOON comes back when you start the truck, repeat the steps.
oil.note: Checked in the 2009 and 2012 owner's manuals.

oil.when: 2011–2012 trucks without Driver Information Center buttons (trip odometer stem)
steps: Reset only after the engine oil and filter have actually been changed.
Shift to Park and turn the ignition on. The oil life reading only shows in Park on these trucks.
Press the trip odometer reset stem until OIL LIFE REMAINING shows.
Press and hold the stem for more than five seconds, until the oil life reads 100%.
If CHANGE ENGINE OIL SOON comes back when you start the truck, repeat the steps.
oil.note: Checked in the 2011 and 2012 owner's manuals.

tpms.when: 2007–2013 when the light came on for low pressure and no wheels were moved
steps: Set all four tires to the cold pressure on the driver's door jamb sticker.
The low tire pressure light and the CHECK TIRE PRESSURE message clear once the pressures are corrected; there is no button to press.
Drive for a few minutes above about 25 mph so the sensors report the new pressures, then check the readings on the Driver Information Center.
If the light stays on, or the display shows SERVICE TIRE MONITOR, a sensor is not reporting and the system needs checking.
tpms.note: The CHECK TIRE PRESSURE message also appears when the spare is in use. If the tire pressure light flashes for about a minute when you start the car and then stays on, the warning system itself has a fault. A reset won't fix it; have it checked.

tpms.when: 2007–2013 sensor relearn after a tire rotation or sensor replacement (key fob or DIC)
steps: Set all four tires to the cold pressure on the driver's door jamb sticker.
Park, set the parking brake, and turn the ignition on with the engine off.
Press and hold the lock and unlock buttons on the key fob together until the horn chirps twice. On trucks without keyless entry, use the DIC information button to reach TIRE LEARN and hold SET/RESET.

The left front turn signal lights. At the driver's front tire, hold a TPMS relearn tool against the tire sidewall near the valve stem and press its button until the horn chirps once. If you don't have the tool, turn the ignition off and have a tire shop do the relearn.
Repeat in this order, waiting for a chirp at each: passenger front, passenger rear, driver rear.
Two chirps after the driver rear tire mean the relearn is done. Turn the ignition off.
Set all four tires back to the door sticker pressure, then drive above about 25 mph for at least two minutes before checking the readings.
tpms.note: Redo the relearn after every rotation or sensor replacement. If SERVICE TIRE MONITOR shows or the light stays on after a completed relearn, the system has a fault a reset will not fix. The twin 2013 Silverado manual uses a relearn tool. Never drive away with a tire you let air out of.

notes: Reset the oil life system after every oil change, even an early one, because it does not reset itself. If it is reset by mistake, change the oil within about 3,000 miles of the last change.
